items.detail: The **Nasdaq closed at a record 27,244**, up 0.5%, while the S&P 500 finished flat at 7,761.
items.why: A renewed chip rally and strong demand for Meta's new AI chatbot revived the AI trade.

items.detail: The **Dow fell 263 points**, or 0.51%, to 51,786, as financial stocks slid nearly 2% against the tech rally.
items.why: Banks sold off while money crowded into AI names, splitting the market between old economy and tech.

items.detail: The **10-year Treasury yield edged back up to about 4.97%** after two Fed officials struck a hawkish tone, with flash PMIs due Wednesday.
items.why: St. Louis Fed's Musalem said more rate increases may be needed to bring inflation back to target.

items.detail: Asian markets stalled after Monday's rally, with **Hong Kong's Hang Seng up just 0.1%** to 26,451 and Shanghai's index up 0.2%.
items.why: Investors are holding fire until Xi's Washington visit and Thursday's summit with Trump.

items.detail: The **Nifty snapped a four-day winning streak**, falling 0.36% to 23,329, while **FIIs sold ₹3,810 crore** of shares.
items.why: Foreign selling ran seven times Monday's pace, and domestic funds' ₹4,120 crore of buying only partly cushioned it.

items.detail: The **Russell 2000 rose 0.51% to 2,889**, the best of the US majors, reversing Monday when it badly lagged the Nasdaq.
items.why: A fifth straight drop in oil helped domestic small caps, which carry heavier fuel and debt costs.

items.detail: **Bitcoin pushed to about $86,600**, its highest since January, lifting the total crypto market back above **$3 trillion**.
items.why: Another $648 million of short positions were liquidated, and the fear and greed gauge jumped to 78.

items.detail: **Ether rose about 5% to roughly $2,776**, and US spot ether ETFs pulled in **$270 million** on the day.
items.why: BlackRock-led institutional buying returned after last week's outflows, the best day for ether funds in six weeks.

items.detail: **Solana climbed toward $120**, its highest since January, after $26 million of ETF inflows extended a 12-week buying run.
items.why: More than $21 million of short positions were wiped out as the token cleared recent resistance.

items.detail: **Spot gold fell about 0.8% to roughly $4,308 an ounce**, a second straight day of losses.
items.why: Hawkish Fed remarks pushed the dollar near a late-July high, denting demand for the non-yielding metal.

crossCuttingTheme: Hawkish Fed talk was the day's lever: it lifted the dollar, hit gold and bank shares and capped the S&P, while a fifth straight fall in oil kept chips and small caps bid.
